To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRAP ECT and A domains are monomeric, bind to HepG2 hepatocytes and have different binding properties.
we have developed procedures for the recombinant production and characterization of TRAP ECD and A domains.
we have produced recombinant TRP domains and characterized their binding properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular determinants that mediate hepatocyte recognition of TRAP, a key step in the malaria parasite invasion process.
the development of recombinant TRAp-based vaccines against malaria.
a detailed analysis of the adhesive properties and structure of TRAP ECD and A domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the A domain of TRP is a ligand for heparin and the ECD of TRP is also a ligand for hepatocytes.
the TRAP A domain is a highly specific and potent ligand for hepatocytes.
TRAP is a complex molecule with multiple ligand-binding surfaces that may play a central role in sporozoite-host cell interaction during the hepatocyte-invasion process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TRAP A domain has a three-dimensional structure very similar to that of the A1 domain of VWF.
we have successfully produced recombinant proteins for TRAP and that they have shown to have biological functions.
the TRAP A domain has a higher affinity for heptarins than the ECD and that it has two spatially distinct binding surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed recombinant procedures for the entire ECD and the adhesive A domain of TRAPII.
the A domain and ECD of TRAP have high-affinity binding to heparin and HepG2 cells respectively.
TRAP EDC and A domain are highly amenable to recombinant production and are amenable to structural studies and functional analysis.
